subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Body Structure and Crumple Zones
description: A short lesson to help you apply Body Structure and Crumple Zones.

hook.text: A strong car body doesn't just protect you in a crash—it also defines how the car handles.

buildup.text: The body shell (unibody) must be stiff enough to keep suspension geometry precise during hard driving.

discovery.text: But in a crash, the front and rear are designed to crumple, absorbing impact before it reaches you.

twist.text: The passenger cabin stays rigid while the surrounding structure collapses in a controlled sequence.

climax.text: High-strength steel and aluminum let modern cars be light, stiff for handling, and safe in a crash.

punchline.text: Cars are built to be stiff where you sit and soft where you don't.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of crumple zones?
options: Absorb crash energy before it reaches passengers
